nodes.title: Outcome and scope
nodes.text: Build a polished, responsive Sudoku web app with Next.js App Router, TypeScript, and client-side state. The MVP lets a player start a puzzle, enter and erase numbers, receive validation feedback, use notes, pause and resume, reset or request a new puzzle, and complete a game with keyboard, pointer, and touch input. It runs without accounts, a database, or a backend.

nodes.title: MVP boundary
nodes.text: Keep the first release focused on a reliable solo puzzle loop and an accessible board.

rows: Easy, medium, hard seeded puzzles; new game
Daily challenges, infinite generation, custom imports
Select cell, enter digit, erase, notes, mistake feedback, pause, completion
Current game and preferences in localStorage
Responsive board, timer, dark mode, sound toggle, undo/redo
Next.js App Router, TypeScript, static/client deployment
Realtime server features and user profiles

nodes.title: Application architecture
nodes.text: Keep Sudoku rules pure and deterministic so the UI can change without changing puzzle correctness.

data.summary: A server-rendered Next.js shell hosts a focused client game boundary, which coordinates accessible input, a pure Sudoku engine, local persistence, and a DOM-based board.

nodes.title: Technical contracts
nodes.text: Define the model and interaction boundaries before visual polish.

rows: Clues never mutate; solution is not exposed to render-only components
Entries, notes, selected cell, mistakes, elapsed time, status
Serializable; every move can be validated and undone
Pure functions; no React, DOM, or localStorage access
Render cells and expose interaction semantics
Each cell has a stable accessible name and selected/conflict state
Save and restore active game and preferences
Versioned payload; corrupt data falls back safely
Never advances while paused or document is hidden

nodes.title: Phased implementation
nodes.text: Complete each phase only after its exit checks pass.

items.label: Phase 1 · Foundation
items.detail: Set up the Next.js App Router project, TypeScript, styling tokens, linting, test tooling, route shell, and initial puzzle fixtures.

items.label: Phase 2 · Pure Sudoku engine
items.detail: Implement grid types, legal-move validation, conflict detection, candidate calculation, completion checks, seeded puzzle loading, and unit tests.

items.label: Phase 3 · Playable board
items.detail: Build the responsive 9x9 board, cell selection, number pad, keyboard navigation, erase, notes mode, mistake feedback, undo/redo, and completion state.

items.label: Phase 4 · Game lifecycle
items.detail: Add difficulty selection, new/reset flows, pause overlay, timer, visibility pause, localStorage restore, first-run instructions, and preference handling.

items.label: Phase 5 · Accessibility and polish
items.detail: Add semantic announcements, visible focus, contrast-safe states, reduced motion, touch targets, mobile safe-area handling, dark mode, and responsive tuning.

items.label: Phase 6 · Verification and release
items.detail: Run unit, component, browser, accessibility, responsive, build, and performance checks; document deployment and known limits.

nodes.title: Delivery dependencies
nodes.text: The dependency order prevents UI behavior from becoming the source of truth for puzzle correctness.

nodes.title: Definition of done
nodes.text: The MVP is complete only when the puzzle loop, accessibility, and resilience gates pass together.

items: Every included puzzle has a valid solution and a unique intended completion path
Clue cells cannot be edited; entries, notes, erase, undo, and redo behave consistently
Conflicts are communicated without relying on color alone, and completion is detected correctly
Keyboard users can navigate the full grid, enter digits, erase, toggle notes, pause, and restart
Touch controls have comfortable targets and work in portrait and landscape layouts
The board, timer, mistakes, pause state, and completion status are available to assistive technology
The active game survives reload; malformed or outdated local data is ignored safely
The timer stops during pause and when the document is hidden
Unit and component tests cover rules, persistence, lifecycle, and critical controls
Playwright covers start, entry, notes, undo, pause, reload, completion, and responsive viewports
Production build completes and the app can deploy as a static/client-only experience

nodes.title: Puzzle correctness and data quality
nodes.text: A bad fixture or generator can produce an unsolvable or ambiguous puzzle and undermine player trust.

data.mitigation: Start with reviewed seeded fixtures, validate each fixture in tests, keep solution and clue data immutable, and isolate any future generator behind the same validation contract.

nodes.title: Accessibility of a dense grid
nodes.text: A visually clear 9x9 board can still be difficult to operate with a keyboard or screen reader.

data.mitigation: Use stable cell semantics and labels, roving or grid keyboard navigation, live status announcements, visible focus, non-color conflict cues, and manual keyboard/screen-reader checks.

nodes.title: Persistence and timer edge cases
nodes.text: Reloads, multiple tabs, clock changes, and hidden documents can create lost games or inflated times.

data.mitigation: Persist a versioned snapshot, derive elapsed time from controlled deltas, pause on visibility change, validate restored state, and define last-write behavior for multiple tabs.

nodes.title: Delivery risk map
nodes.text: Correctness and accessible interaction deserve earlier validation than decorative polish.

data.summary: Puzzle correctness and dense-grid accessibility have the highest combined delivery risk; persistence edge cases are important but narrower.

nodes.title: Testing strategy
nodes.text: Use Vitest for pure Sudoku rules, fixture validation, candidate calculation, completion, and persistence serialization. Use React Testing Library for selection, input modes, announcements, pause, and toolbar behavior. Use Playwright for complete browser flows at 375, 768, 1024, and 1440 CSS pixels, including keyboard-only and touch-emulated runs. Add axe checks, production-build verification, and a small performance check to ensure typing never causes avoidable whole-page rerenders.

nodes.title: Explicit non-goals
nodes.text: Do not add authentication, databases, online multiplayer, analytics tracking, ads, chat, payments, or a large global state library in the MVP. A puzzle generator, hints, daily challenges, and social features should follow only after the local game loop is stable and measured.

nodes.title: Recommended delivery approach
nodes.text: Ship a local-first Sudoku MVP around a pure TypeScript engine and a semantic DOM grid. Use Next.js for the route shell and deployment, keep interactive state inside a narrow client boundary, begin with validated seeded puzzles, and make keyboard/touch/accessibility behavior part of every phase gate.

nodes.title: Implementation scope decision
nodes.text: Approve the plan before creating the Next.js application and game modules.
